     1	# Linux Package Sources: apt vs Linuxbrew vs snap vs GitHub binaries
     2	
     3	This repo mixes several package sources on Linux. This document explains what each is good at, the trade-offs, and the policy the ansible roles follow.
     4	
     5	These package managers are **complementary, not substitutes**. Picking the right source for a tool is what keeps this dotfiles setup fast, portable, and safe across `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`, and `noRoot` profiles.
     6	
     7	## Side-by-side comparison
     8	
     9	| Dimension | apt | snap | Linuxbrew | GitHub binary |
    10	|---|---|---|---|---|
    11	| Version freshness | Poor (LTS freeze) | Medium–Good | **Good** (near-upstream) | Good |
    12	| Sudo required | Yes | Yes (+ snapd daemon, needs systemd) | Yes at install (chown `/home/linuxbrew`) | **No** |
    13	| Cross-platform with macOS | Linux-only | Linux-only | **Same formula names as macOS Homebrew** | If upstream ships binaries |
    14	| Sandboxing | None | **AppArmor + strict interfaces** | None | None |
    15	| Startup / resource cost | Lowest | High (squashfs mount + bundled libs per snap) | Medium (bottles ship own lib paths) | Lowest |
    16	| System services / daemons | **Best** | OK but constrained by confinement | Poor (`brew services` on Linux is experimental) | Manual |
    17	| Catalog breadth | Largest | Medium (GUI-heavy) | Strong for CLI / dev tools | One tool per source |
    18	| Upgrade control | Ships with distro upgrades | Auto-refresh (hard to disable cleanly) | Explicit `brew upgrade` (rolling) | Manual / ansible-driven |
    19	| Disk footprint | Small (shared libs) | Large (redundant libs, retains prev. revisions) | Medium (~/.linuxbrew 10–15 GB common) | Small |
    20	| Breakage risk | Low (distro maintainers vetted) | Medium (silent refresh can change behaviour) | Low (rolling, explicit) | Low |
    21	| Works in `noRoot` mode | ❌ | ❌ (snapd needs sudo + systemd) | ⚠️ Unsupported `~/homebrew` mode exists but loses bottles → needs `libevent-dev` etc. → circles back to sudo | ✅ |
    22	
    23	## Pick-by-tool-type
    24	
    25	| Tool type | Preferred source | Why |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| Modern CLI dev tools (tmux, neovim, ripgrep, fd, zoxide, starship, eza, yazi, sesh, television) | **Linuxbrew** if sudo available; **GitHub binary** in `noRoot` | Freshest versions, shared formula names with macOS `Brewfile.darwin`, no confinement friction |
    28	| System daemons / kernel or systemd-adjacent tools (Docker Engine, OpenSSH server, NetworkManager, CUDA, nvidia drivers) | **apt** | snap sandbox fights with host-integrated daemons; brew has no story for system services on Linux |
    29	| Sandboxed or closed-source GUI (Slack, some IDEs, Bitwarden Desktop) | **snap** / flatpak / vendor `.deb` | brew-linux has no cask; apt versions lag; snap's automatic updates + confinement are a fit |
    30	| Language runtimes (Node, Python, Ruby, Rust) | **mise** (already used) | Multi-version, project-aware, user-level — beats every OS package manager for this job |
    31	| Language-ecosystem CLI tools (`uv tool`, `gem`, `cargo install`, `npm -g`) | **Language tool** | Latest upstream, auto-resolves ecosystem deps, installs to user prefix |
    32	| Fully no-sudo environment | **GitHub binary + mise + language tools** | The `noRoot=true` branch of this repo |
    33	
    34	## Linuxbrew vs apt
    35	
    36	**Prefer Linuxbrew when:**
    37	
    38	- The tool is also installed on macOS (shared mental model with `Brewfile.darwin`).
    39	- The apt version is too old for the repo's config (e.g. tmux: Ubuntu 22.04 ships 3.2a, but our popup menu needs ≥ 3.3 — see [tools/tmux/README.md](tools/tmux/README.md)).
    40	- You want explicit, rolling upgrades rather than waiting for the next distro release.
    41	
    42	**Stay on apt when:**
    43	
    44	- The tool is a system daemon or needs PAM / systemd / `/etc/shells` integration (e.g. `zsh`, `openssh-server`, `docker.io`).
    45	- The machine is disk-constrained — apt shares system libs, brew ships its own stack.
    46	- Unattended security updates matter more than version freshness.
    47	
    48	## Linuxbrew vs snap
    49	
    50	These cover different surfaces. If the choice is forced:
    51	
    52	- **CLI tools → Linuxbrew.** snap-confined CLIs frequently hit issues reading `~/.config`, `~/.ssh`, `/tmp`, or other dotfiles because of AppArmor interface rules. Slow startup (squashfs mount + confinement enforce) is also noticeable for tools invoked often.
    53	- **GUI apps → snap.** Fits the confinement model, auto-update works well for interactive apps that don't need deep filesystem access.
    54	
    55	## Repo policy
    56	
    57	Summarising how the ansible roles route tool installs:
    58	
    59	```
    60	macOS:
    61	  Homebrew (CLI + cask), mas for A
... (truncated)

   270	    # Check if collection is already installed (e.g. network blocked by GFW)
   271	    if ansible-galaxy collection list community.general 2>/dev/null | grep -q community.general; then
   272	        warn "Galaxy download failed but community.general is already installed, continuing..."
   273	    else
   274	        error "Failed to install community.general collection. Ansible playbooks will not work."
   275	        error "Try setting: export https_proxy=http://your-proxy:port"
   276	        exit 1
   277	    fi
   278	fi

   280	# 6. Install mise global tools (Node.js) if mise config exists
   281	MISE_BIN="${HOME}/.local/bin/mise"
   282	[[ ! -x "$MISE_BIN" ]] && MISE_BIN="$(command -v mise 2>/dev/null || true)"
   283	if [[ -x "$MISE_BIN" ]] && [[ -f "$HOME/.config/mise/config.toml" ]]; then
   284	    info "Installing mise global tools..."
   285	    if "$MISE_BIN" install --yes; then
   286	        success "mise tools installed"
   287	    else
   288	        warn "mise install had errors (some tools may have failed to build). Continuing..."
   289	    fi
   290	fi
   291	
   292	# 7. Ensure ~/.local/bin is on PATH for bash sessions (idempotent)
   293	# chezmoi, uv, mise all live in ~/.local/bin. Dotfiles only wire this up in
   294	# zsh; until the user switches shells, bash needs help finding them.
   295	BASHRC="$HOME/.bashrc"
   296	LOCAL_BIN_LINE='export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"'
   297	if [[ -f "$BASHRC" ]] || [[ "${SHELL##*/}" == "bash" ]]; then
   298	    touch "$BASHRC"
   299	    if ! grep -qF "$LOCAL_BIN_LINE" "$BASHRC"; then
   300	        {
   301	            echo ""
   302	            echo "# Added by chezmoi bootstrap - ~/.local/bin for uv, mise, chezmoi"
   303	            echo "$LOCAL_BIN_LINE"
   304	        } >> "$BASHRC"
   305	        info "Added ~/.local/bin to PATH in $BASHRC"
   306	    fi
   307	fi

   309	success "Bootstrap complete!"

**現況**

大致上是，你的理解沒錯: 目前這套 **不是自動更新器**，比較像「宣告式安裝 + 缺什麼補什麼」。

- `chezmoi apply` 不會每次都重跑 ansible。ansible phase 是 [`run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:1)，只有 role/default 檔內容變了才會觸發；Brewfile 也是類似邏輯，在 [`run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl:1)。
- 就算 ansible 有重跑，多數 task 也只是 `state: present`，意思是「確保已安裝」，不是「升到最新版」。例如 [`dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:4) 跟 [`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:15)。
- Brewfile 路徑更明確: 它直接跑 `brew bundle --no-upgrade`，所以 brew bundle 管的 app/cli 不會自動升版，看 [`run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl:126)。
- `uv tool` / `cargo install` 這些很多都用了 `creates:`，本質上是 install-once。例子: [`python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml:5)、[`rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml:18)。
- npm 類也大多是 `state: present` 或「只裝缺的」，不是 upgrade 流程。例子: [`js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml:73)、[`bitwarden/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml:78)。
- 少數例外有升級傾向。macOS 的 Neovim 是 `state: latest`，看 [`neovim/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/neovim/tasks/main.yml:19)。Homebrew 本身也會 `update_homebrew: true`，但那是更新 brew metadata，不是全面升 formula，看 [`homebrew/tasks/main.yml`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/homebrew/tasks/main.yml:25)。
- `chezmoiexternal` 是另一條線，這個會每週 refresh upstream clone，不靠 ansible。看 [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl:7)。

**Comment**

我覺得這個設計對 dotfiles repo 是合理的，因為 `chezmoi apply` 最怕的是順手把整台機器升到一堆新版本，然後引入不可預期 breakage。現在的策略偏保守、可重現。

但缺點也很明顯: 「安裝」跟「更新」語義目前有點混。repo 裡同時有 `present`、`latest`、`creates`、missing-only 幾種模式，所以使用者不太容易預期哪些工具會前進、哪些會卡在初裝版本。像 README 寫 mise `ensures latest versions`，如果解讀成「之後會持續跟上最新版」，其實偏樂觀了，看 [`README.md`](/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/README.md:198)。

我會建議把它拆成兩條路:

- `chezmoi apply` / ansible default: 維持現在這種保守 install-only 行為。
- 另外做一個明確的 upgrade 入口，例如 `just upgrade-tools` 或一個 ansible tag，專門跑 `brew upgrade`、拿掉 `brew bundle --no-upgrade`、`mise upgrade`、`uv tool upgrade --all`、`dotnet tool update --global` 等。

這樣會比「每次 apply 順便升級全部」乾淨很多。如果你要，我可以直接幫你把這個 repo 補成一套 `just upgrade-tools` / `just update-all` 的明確升級流。
